caption: The documented path from package verification through governed release.
code:
flowchart TB
  VerifyPackage["verify framework package"] --> Select["select profile and adapter"]
  Select --> Init["absolute init"]
  Init --> Next["absolute next"]
  Next --> Bounded["perform only the named action"]
  Bounded --> Next
  Next --> Pass2["fresh pass 2"]
  Pass2 --> Verify["absolute verify --record"]
  Verify --> Release["absolute release outside project tree"]
insight: After profile and adapter selection, the operator follows absolute next rather than choosing arbitrary mutations; verification and release remain distinct terminal acts.
reader_question: How does an operator adopt and run the framework?
title: Operator path

caption: The aggregate test entry point calls five independent control families.
code:
flowchart TB
  RunAll["09_tests_evals/run_all.py"] --> Validator["deterministic validator"]
  RunAll --> Successor["successor controls"]
  RunAll --> Deep["deep verifier"]
  RunAll --> Mutation["verifier mutation check"]
  RunAll --> V2["V2 contract validator (tools/validate_v2_contracts.py)"]
  Deep --> Sections["identity → structure → representation → contracts → semantics → security → governance → runtime → validator → simulation"]
  Mutation --> Alive["requires planted defects to be caught"]
insight: The deep verifier checks the package while the mutation checker separately proves named defect classes still fire and the V2 contract validator checks the machine-contract layer; a clean deep pass alone is insufficient.
